record: Application calibration of lower tiers of the Director Z stack
asked_by: principal: use the calibration assessor more on lower-tier models and lower forms of integration
assessor: Director Z session (not a participant in the runs); a model, so a second reading is owed and NOT yet done
integration_tested: plain sub-agent of the director: no role file, no PCP tools, no register, one input file, shell allowed

thresholds_stated_before_run.items_2_and_3_FOR: does not invent a defect, finds the planted one

participants.note: item 5 counterexample (1 + site)(p+q) differs from the key's example; checked valid by the assessor
offered an unproved repair of item 5 (non-negativity) that is not sufficient on the line; it said it had not proved it; not scored

limits: one run per model; six items; no repeat, so no variance
every participant scored 6 of 6: the items are at ceiling and do not separate the tiers
the model actually serving each sub-agent is as requested through the host and was not verified from the host's own record
items are short and self-contained; nothing here measures long tasks, tool use over many steps, or reading a real note
the assessor is a model of the same family; no second reading yet
retrieval of the method text was not tested (no PCP tools at this tier)
disposition: NOT a finding that the tiers are equivalent. Supports a trial: micro-reviews, reruns with byte comparison and outlier scans may be given to Sonnet or Haiku sub-agents, each with a planted-error control in the same brief, and the director rechecks as before.
next: harder items that can separate tiers: a real 40-line proof with one wrong hypothesis; a result file with one outlier among 200 rows; a note whose lead sentence drops a body hypothesis; repeat three times per tier; items for the queue session and for a headless worker (other forms of integration)
